title: Argentina's Prefectura Naval intercepts the Vanuatu-flagged XINRUN 579 on 5 January 2025 after Skylight speed-range and machine-learning fishing alerts; Skylight reports a fine was paid
summary: PNA intercepted XINRUN 579 fishing illegally in Argentina's EEZ on 5 Jan 2025; Skylight says its speed-range and ML fishing alerts prompted the response and a first electronic fine was paid.
account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579 inside Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots, which local rules treat as an indication of trawling; the coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it and the captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025: a rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities, a Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model followed 40 minutes later, PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel, and the case led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid; it quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI; the PNA press release that Skylight links to returns 404 live and in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.
purpose: Real-time detection of suspicious vessel behavior and fishing activity to support maritime enforcement against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing; the interception was the intended use.
system: Skylight maritime-monitoring platform (Speed Range Event rule and machine-learning Fishing Event detection)
deployer: Prefectura Naval Argentina (Dirección de Tráfico Marítimo, Fluvial y Lacustre; EICEMAR)
location: Argentine exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, Argentina
domain: Fisheries enforcement / illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
segment: National coastguard using a free non-profit AI platform
taxonomy_note: Loose fit: the benefit is an enforcement action and fine protecting a squid and hake fishery; no catch or ecological harm avoided is quantified. The AI role rests on Skylight's own account, including the PNA officers it quotes; the one independent news report credits the PNA monitoring system and does not mention Skylight.

ratings.reason: The PNA intercepted the vessel within hours and, per Skylight, issued its first international electronic fine with the fine and costs paid; the independent report confirms the interception and administrative proceedings.
One vessel among hundreds operating at the edge of Argentina's EEZ each season; the fishery-level effect is not quantified.

ai_role.statement: Skylight's own account describes a two-stage AI contribution: a rule-based Speed Range Event flagged the vessel at under 6 knots inside an area of interest, and 40 minutes later a Fishing Event from its machine-learning model, which detects longlining, trawling and squid jigging, reinforced the suspicion before PNA analysts redirected a coastguard vessel; a retired PNA captain is quoted saying Skylight contributed directly to the decision. This is the maker's account, with the deployer's officers quoted inside it. The independent report (Agenda Malvinas, citing Pescare and official information) attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not name Skylight or AI, so the attribution to the AI output is not independently confirmed; the PNA release Skylight links to could not be fetched.
